thread:
marta: Heads-up — I'm about to open a migration PR for the console_metrics table. goal is to split heavy aggregation fields into metrics_v3 while keeping read adapters for the console so visualizations don't break.

samir: nice. can you include a compatibility layer? i want the UI to keep querying /v1/metrics for the next 6 weeks while we roll out.

marta: yep planning a read-adapter service that maps old envelope -> v3 columns. adapter will live in ingest-proxy and have a feature flag. basic plan: dual-write for 48h in staging, then shadow-write for 7 days in prod, then cutover.

tyler: two quick asks: 1) what's the index strategy for the v3 key shapes? 2) any queries in the console that will become much slower during backfill?

marta: index strategy: composite (tenant_id, metric_name, time_bucket) + sparse index for high-cardinality tags. backfill will touch ~18B rows; we will do chunked backfill by tenant windows and throttle via ingest-proxy rate limiter.

olivia: we should also gate the adapter behind a routing policy for enterprise tenants — they care about SLA and we shouldn't risk extra latency.

marta: agreed. plan is: routing policy picks preferred_store = {metrics_v3, metrics_v2}, fallback to v2 if v3 under capacity. that lets we can move tenants over gradually.

jui: small UX note — the dashboard boolean for "show historic anomalies" currently queries the wide row pattern; if we change the storage shape it might need a different pre-aggregation. can we keep the old pre-agg API until the migration finalizes?

samir: yeah keep the API contract stable. we can add a thin facade that serves pre-agg from cached time-series if v3 path doesn't have it yet.

engflow-bot: migration-checklist created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/migrations/metrics_v3.checklist — items: schema-migration, index-build, shadow-write, backfill-run, canary-cutover.

marta: checklist link is the source of truth. I'll add safepoints for each phase with SQL and pg_replay steps. also adding a query-contract test harness that runs against both stores and asserts parity for a sample of queries.

tyler: how do you plan to measure parity? token counts? metric_bucket sums? we need a tolerance because of eventual-consistency during shadow-write.

marta: parity checks: row-count delta < 0.05% for aggregated windows, bucket_sum diff < 0.5% for >1000 count windows. tests will run nightly and on every backfill chunk completion.

jui: for alerting, add a regression alert to the console that watches the "top-10 widgets" latency and an accuracy metric derived from parity tests.

olivia: and add an opt-out for orgs that want to postpone migration — persistent toggle on account record + migration schedule field. ops can delay for compliance reasons.

samir: operational question: will queries go cross-region for some tenants during backfill? that's a big latency risk.

marta: we'll avoid cross-region reads. backfill workers will run in-region and the adapter will prefer local v3 shards. if a tenant has mixed-region data we'll mark them for a manual cutover.

tyler: please document expected additional egress >0 in the PR. infra needs numbers for capacity planning.

marta: will do. rough estimate: peak inbound write amplification ~1.15x during shadow-write, backfill reads ~200MB/s sustained for the largest 20 tenants.

jui: one more: console telemetry fields that record query fingerprint + selected_filters. We'll add a version field so older dashboards still map. don't rename the telemetry keys.

marta: yep will append telemetry_version and keep existing keys.

olivia: timeline?

marta: draft PR today, integration tests + adapter by EOW, shadow-write in staging next week, prod shadow-write 2w after, progressive tenant migration over 6 weeks.

samir: sounds good. assign me to the cutover runbook and me+tyler will own the canary phase.

marta: perfect. I'll post the runbook here when PR lands. thanks all :thumbsup:

engflow-bot: deploy: ingest-proxy/adapter canary queued for staging (id: dpl-4921).

tyler: received. I'll watch staging traces and the console metrics latency board. :eyes:

marta: closing thread for now — will reopen with runbook link once PR is up.
